definition: Truncate means to shorten by cutting off part of something.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word truncate. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know truncate should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Budget cuts truncated the pier by forty feet, and the pavilion planned for its end was never built.
Trim is milder — a snip here and there with the shape kept whole; to truncate is to lop the whole end off.
Gut goes further than truncate: not just the tail cut away but the middle hollowed out, until only a shell of the original remains.

Shorten is the all-purpose word: a thing ends up shorter by any means at all — compressing, thinning, cutting. Truncate is one specific way of shortening: the loss comes off an end, usually in a single blunt cut, and the shape shows it.

Clip means to snip a small, tidy piece off an edge — a coupon, a hedge, a loose thread. Truncate is the heavier act: a whole end lopped off at once, leaving the thing visibly incomplete rather than neatly groomed.

Truncate is blunt and slightly technical — fields truncate long names, frost truncates seasons, editors truncate columns.
The cut always comes off an end, often crudely.
